name: BC Home Energy Improvement Bonus
runBy: CleanBC / Better Homes BC, with BC Hydro and FortisBC
auditRequirementNote: Built entirely around the audit: a pre-retrofit and a post-retrofit EnerGuide evaluation by an NRCan-registered energy advisor bracket the work, and the bonus pays on the measured improvement between the two.
headline: $20 for every percentage-point your home improves — $750 minimum, $2,000 maximum, province-wide since May 2026

amounts.label: Per percentage-point of measured EnerGuide improvement

whoQualifies: BC homeowners who complete at least three eligible upgrades with a pre- and post-retrofit EnerGuide evaluation. It stacks on top of the individual utility rebates for the upgrades themselves — the bonus pays for the measured whole.
notes: This is the purest pay-for-performance design in Canada right now: the more your blower-door number and EnerGuide rating actually move, the more it pays. Sequence air sealing before insulation and you earn the same dollars twice — once in the bonus, once on your bills.
howToApply: Book a pre-retrofit EnerGuide evaluation with an NRCan-registered energy advisor before any work starts — this sets your baseline rating.
Plan at least three eligible upgrades from the evaluation report (air sealing, insulation, windows, heating — the report ranks them for your house).
Complete the work, keeping invoices, and claim the individual utility rebates for each measure as you go.
Book the post-retrofit evaluation with the same advisor to measure the new rating.
Submit the bonus claim with both evaluation files — payment scales with the measured percentage-point improvement.
gotchas: No pre-retrofit evaluation, no bonus — work done before the baseline visit doesn't count, so book the audit first, not after the contractor.
Three upgrades is the floor for eligibility; below that the bonus pays nothing even if your rating improves.
The $2,000 cap means very deep retrofits don't earn past 100 points of improvement — but the utility measure rebates still apply on top.
Income-qualified households should check the CleanBC Energy Savings Program first — free installs beat rebates.

faq.q: Is the BC Home Energy Improvement Bonus available everywhere in BC?
faq.a: Yes — it went province-wide on May 15, 2026 after starting as a regional offer. Any BC home that completes the pre/post evaluations and three or more eligible upgrades can claim it, verified against Better Homes BC on September 18, 2026.

faq.q: How much is the bonus actually worth for a typical retrofit?
faq.a: It pays $20 per percentage-point of measured EnerGuide improvement, between $750 and $2,000. A meaningful envelope package — air sealing plus attic and basement insulation — on an older home routinely moves the rating enough to land in the upper half of that range, and the pre-retrofit evaluation report will estimate your specific potential.

faq.q: Does it stack with BC Hydro and FortisBC rebates?
faq.a: Yes — the per-measure utility rebates apply to the individual upgrades, and the bonus pays separately on the whole-home improvement the evaluations measure. Stack both; they're designed together under the Better Homes BC umbrella.

notes: Quebec splits the file in two: Rénoclimat = envelope (audit required), LogisVert = equipment (no audit). Plan both together — insulate and air-seal under Rénoclimat first, then size the LogisVert heat pump to the improved house. A flooding-adaptation component joins the program October 1, 2026.
howToApply: Register with Rénoclimat by phone or online — the program assigns an authorized evaluator to your home (about $150 + tax).
Get the evaluation and its report: your home's rating plus the ranked envelope measures.
Complete eligible work (insulation, air sealing, doors/windows) with proper invoices.

faq.q: Is Rénoclimat still active, and what does it cost to start?
faq.a: Active — verified against the Quebec government page on September 21, 2026. Your cost of entry is the evaluation at roughly $150 + tax, with an evaluator assigned by the program rather than chosen by you.

faq.q: What's the difference between Rénoclimat and LogisVert?
faq.a: Rénoclimat is the province's audit-linked envelope program: insulation, air sealing, doors and windows, with pre/post evaluations. LogisVert is Hydro-Québec's equipment program — heat pumps, appliances, solar — with no audit required. A serious retrofit uses both, in that order.

faq.q: What's changing on October 1, 2026?

name: Hydro-Québec LogisVert
auditRequirementNote: No audit required — grants apply directly to eligible equipment. An EnerGuide or Rénoclimat evaluation is still the smart first step so the heat pump gets sized to an improved envelope, not the leaky one.
headline: Heat pump grants scaled to capacity — $50–$120 per 1,000 BTU/h — plus appliances and solar, no audit needed
whoQualifies: Hydro-Québec residential customers installing eligible equipment. Grants are claimed per measure; several are handled by the installer directly on the invoice.
notes: The roof-insulation-and-caulking measure ended August 25, 2025 — envelope money now lives entirely with Rénoclimat. LogisVert remains the fastest equipment money in the country: no audit gate, and capacity-scaled heat pump grants that reward proper (not oversized) sizing.
howToApply: Confirm the model is on the eligible list (ENERGY STAR certification is mandatory for heat pumps installed after November 26, 2025).
Get a real heat-loss calculation before quotes — the grant scales with capacity, but oversizing still costs you comfort and efficiency.
Install through a qualified contractor; several measures are credited by the installer on the invoice.
Submit remaining claims through your Hydro-Québec account with the invoices.
Pair with Rénoclimat for the envelope side — the two programs are designed as a set.
gotchas: Non-ENERGY STAR heat pumps installed after November 26, 2025 get nothing — check the model number before signing.
Roof insulation left LogisVert in August 2025; contractors still quoting it under LogisVert are working from stale information (our standing trust test).
Grant-per-BTU can tempt oversizing — the F280 heat-loss calculation is your defence, and our guide covers it.

faq.q: How much does LogisVert pay for a heat pump?
faq.a: Between $50 and $120 per 1,000 BTU/h of capacity depending on the system type and efficiency, verified against Hydro-Québec's page September 21, 2026 — a typical properly-sized wall-mounted system lands in the low thousands. ENERGY STAR certification is required for installs after November 26, 2025.

faq.q: Does LogisVert require an energy audit?
faq.a: No — it's Quebec's no-audit equipment stream. But sizing the heat pump from a CSA F280 heat-loss calculation (ideally after Rénoclimat envelope work) is what makes the equipment actually perform; the grant pays either way, your comfort doesn't.

faq.q: Can I still get LogisVert money for insulation?
faq.a: No — the roof insulation and caulking measure ended August 25, 2025. Envelope rebates run through Rénoclimat now; LogisVert covers equipment, appliances and solar.

faq.q: Is the Saskatchewan Home Efficiency Retrofit Rebate still available?
faq.a: No — it ended in April 2026 (verified September 18, 2026) and no replacement has been announced. Rotating SaskEnergy and SaskPower equipment offers are what remain.

faq.q: What can Saskatchewan homeowners get right now?
faq.a: Utility equipment offers (check both utilities' current lists), and the pure-physics return on audit-guided envelope work — which in Saskatchewan's climate is among the best in the country even unsubsidized.

faq.q: Why list a dead program at all?
faq.a: Because stale advertising outlives programs by years, and knowing a promise is dead is worth as much as knowing a program is live. A contractor citing this rebate in 2026 has told you how current the rest of their pitch is.

faq.q: What energy programs exist in Canada's territories?
faq.a: Yukon's Good Energy rebates (retrofits, renewables, transport), the NWT's Arctic Energy Alliance (rebates and free advice), and Nunavut Housing Corporation homeowner support — each verified active September 21, 2026. Streams change with funding years, so the organizations' current lists govern.

faq.q: Do heat pumps work in the territories?
faq.a: Cold-climate models keep improving, but at −40 design temperatures equipment choice is genuinely specialized — this is exactly what the Arctic Energy Alliance and Yukon's Energy Branch advise on. Get northern-specific advice before any quote, and treat southern marketing claims with suspicion.

faq.q: Why do audits matter more in the North?
faq.a: Because fuel can cost several times southern prices, every air leak and thin assembly the audit finds is worth multiples of its southern value — and because envelope failures at northern temperatures are safety issues, not comfort issues.
